name: VA Cooperative BPH
aliases: Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Study Group
question: Do terazosin, finasteride, or their combination improve symptoms and peak urinary flow more than placebo in men with symptomatic BPH?

design.population: 1,229 men with symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods; PubMed publication types and MeSH

verdictNote: Terazosin improved both endpoints; finasteride and its addition to terazosin did not.
takeaway: Over one year, terazosin 10 mg daily improved symptom scores and peak urinary flow versus placebo in men with BPH; finasteride 5 mg daily did not, and adding it to terazosin gave no additional benefit.

reports.label: Primary symptom and flow report
reports.citation: Lepor H, Williford WO, Barry MJ, et al. "The Efficacy of Terazosin, Finasteride, or Both in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *N Engl J Med.* 1996;335(8):533-540. doi:10.1056/NEJM199608223350801

results.measure: Mean decrease from baseline at 1 year, points

effect.p: <0.001 for terazosin and combination versus finasteride and placebo

results.note: Finasteride did not differ from placebo; combination was no more effective than terazosin alone.

results.measure: Mean increase from baseline at 1 year, mL/s

effect.p: <0.001 for terazosin and combination versus finasteride and placebo

results.note: Finasteride did not differ from placebo; combination was no more effective than terazosin alone.

harms.label: Discontinuation because of adverse effects
harms.note: 1.6% with placebo versus 4.8%-7.8% across the three active groups; the abstract gives no arm-specific rates or denominators.

values.combo: both drugs at the assigned doses

reports.label: Symptom bother and quality of life
reports.citation: Lepor H, Williford WO, Barry MJ, et al. "The impact of medical therapy on bother due to symptoms, quality of life and global outcome, and factors predicting response." *J Urol.* 1998;160(4):1358-1367. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(01)62536-9
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Patient followup, p 1359

results.measure: Marked or moderate global improvement at 52 weeks; final-visit respondents
results.note: The paper tests any improvement versus none or worse, not the marked-or-moderate dichotomy; percentages here are descriptive.

results.measure: Any global improvement versus none or worse at 52 weeks; final-visit respondents

effect.p: terazosin vs placebo 0.025; combination vs placebo 0.001; finasteride vs placebo 0.497; combination vs terazosin 0.235

results.note: Chi-square tests compare any improvement with no improvement or worse.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 1360; Table 3, p 1361

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at 52 weeks, points; final-visit observations

effect.p: repeated measures through 52 weeks: terazosin vs placebo <0.0001; combination vs placebo <0.0001; finasteride vs placebo 0.7504; combination vs terazosin 1.0000

results.note: Analyses included all randomized men with any follow-up data in assigned arms; final-visit denominators vary by endpoint. No confidence interval reported for these arm changes.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Statistical analysis, p 1359; Tables 1-2, pp 1360-1361

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at 52 weeks, points; final-visit observations

effect.p: repeated measures through 52 weeks: terazosin vs placebo <0.0001; combination vs placebo <0.0001; finasteride vs placebo 0.7318; combination vs terazosin 1.0000

results.note: No confidence interval reported for these arm changes.

results.endpoint: Peak flow in men with baseline prostate volume >50 cm3
results.measure: Mean change from baseline at 52 weeks, mL/s; subgroup with baseline and 52-week measurements
results.note: Finasteride versus placebo showed no significant difference in AUA symptom, symptom problem, or BPH impact scores in this subgroup; 17% of study participants had baseline prostate volume >50 cm3.
results.locator: Full text, Tables 6-7, p 1363; Results, p 1361; Discussion, p 1364

delivery.label: Terazosin titration and dose reduction
delivery.value: Terazosin or matching placebo at bedtime: 1 mg days 1-3, 2 mg days 4-7, 5 mg days 8-14, then 10 mg from day 15; terazosin could be reduced to 5 mg for an attributed adverse effect. Finasteride or matching placebo was 5 mg nightly.
delivery.note: All arms received matching placebos; protocol allowed blinded dose reduction.

reports.label: PSA response analysis
reports.citation: Brawer MK, Lin DW, Williford WO, et al. "Effect of finasteride and/or terazosin on serum PSA: results of VA Cooperative Study #359." *Prostate.* 1999;39(4):234-239. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0045(19990601)39:4<234::AID-PROS3>3.0.CO;2-4

results.measure: Direction of PSA change at 52 weeks
results.note: Terazosin did not differ from placebo. Only 35% of men receiving finasteride or combination had the expected 40%-60% PSA decrease; the abstract does not give a pooled denominator.
